Subject: [Urgent] Private cluster degradation since model upgrade (high p95 + 5xx)

Hi Jonas,

We started seeing a sharp regression in tail latency and an increase in 500s on our private VPC deployment after the model refresh you pushed on 2028-02-25 at ~18:00 UTC. Quick summary of what we're observing: 

- p95 generation latency jumped from ~180ms -> ~1.8s over the last 12 hours.
- Throughput (inference QPS) dropped ~35-45% at peak; queue lengths grew on our side.
- Intermittent 5xx during decode stage (502/504) — looks correlated with longer context requests.
- This is affecting our real-time recommendations pipeline; downstream timeouts are triggering.

I've attached a metrics dump and a few sample request IDs (in the zip). We haven't changed client-side batching or max_seq_len on our end. The only change in the window was the model variant rollout from you.

We need immediate help — this is customer-impacting. Can you escalate and advise mitigations we can apply in the private cluster now? Our CTO Nina Rao is copied.

Attachments: silverpine_metrics_20280226.zip

Thanks,
Sam Tucker

Subject: INTERNAL: Silverpine private cluster — immediate triage request (SUP-4721)

Grace / Marissa,

We're getting an urgent P1 from Silverpine (private VPC). Symptoms: large jump in p95 (~180ms -> ~1.8s), throughput drop, intermittent 502/504 during decode. Customer rolled the day-before model variant OTA (2028-02-25 ~18:00 UTC). Artifacts attached by customer: silverpine_metrics_20280226.zip (contains Prometheus slices + sample request IDs).

Immediate asks (please prioritize now):
- Grace: run the KV cache profiler on the customer's cluster snapshot they provided; I suspect KV cache thrash + eviction storms due to a shift to longer sequences in production. See attached kvcache_profiler_20280226.txt.
- Marissa: check kernel selection logs — we may be dropping into a slow attention path when seq_len > 1024; confirm whether compilation/kernel fallback occurred after the variant change.
- Both: check batching window and observed batch sizes over the last 6 hours; if average batch latency spiked, that might explain the p95.

Proposed quick mitigations to consider (customer-approved safe changes):
- Reduce batching window from current value -> 4ms to lower tail latency.
- Increase KV cache allocation to 2x (if memory headroom exists in their private node pool).
- If kernel fallback is observed, pin routing to previous model variant for the hot routes (rollback if safe).

Customer gives read-only logs access if we request it — Sam will confirm. I've opened SUP-4721 and added the metrics link: https://drive.redwood.com/s/silverpine/metrics-20280226.

Please reply with triage findings and ETA. I'm prepping an exec note depending on severity.

— Jonas

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 26 Feb 2028 11:04:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Silverpine private cluster — immediate triage request (SUP-4721)

Quick update from triage:

Findings (preliminary):
- KV cache profiler (attached) shows rapid evictions starting ~2028-02-25T18:10:00Z, coincident with the customer's rollout window. Eviction rate increased ~6x. Workload traces show a higher proportion (~22% -> 48%) of longer contexts (seq_len > 800).
- Kernel selection logs indicate multiple fallbacks to the slower attention path for longer sequences; the compiled kernel for the new variant uses different tiling that performs poorly on their current GPU firmware.
- Observed batch size growth intermittently; when longer contexts arrive we see batch coalescing that increases per-batch decode time and pushes p95 up.

Short-term mitigation we can apply (customer approved):
1) Force model pin to previous variant for the critical route(s) (risk: small regression in quality).
2) Drop batching window to 4ms and cap batch size to reduce tail effects.
3) Increase KV cache size / adjust eviction policy to LRU+pin for recent prefixes.

I attached a proposed rollout plan: silverpine_rollout_plan_20280228.md with step-by-step commands and rollback steps. If exec agrees, we can do the config-only mitigations in ~30-90 minutes. The model pin/rollback requires a slightly longer window ~3-4 hours to validate.

We should also consider a more durable fix: recompile the attention kernel for the customer's GPU firmware and ship a micro-optimized build — that's a 1-2 week engineering task.

ETA for config push: 45 minutes (if Jonass gets read-only logs and confirms permission).

— Grace O'Connor
Senior Site Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
